That relief is a good sign — it means the sentence fits you. The "then I shut up" part is fine too, as long as you don't shut down; let her respond, even if it's awkward.

If she jumps to offering money, you can keep it simple: "I don't need you to fix it — I just needed to say it." Then you're still the one who said the true thing, not the cousin who took the money. Get some sleep; the sentence will keep.
